Digestion of carbohydrates occurs in the mouth as it contains amylase i.e. carbohydrate digesting enzyme. The stomach releases the pepsin enzyme, which is protein-digesting and hence protein digestion takes place in the stomach and also in the small intestine. Lipid or the fat digestion begins in the stomach with the gastric lipase. However, the bulk of lipid digestion occurs in the small intestine due to pancreatic lipase. However, the small intestine is the site of the complete digestion of nucleic acids. Nucleic acids like DNA and RNA in food get digested in the small intestine with the help of pancreatic enzymes and the small intestine enzymes like ribonuclease and deoxyribonuclease.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Innermost mucosa layer of a small intestine has mucosal epithelium which is modified to form the intestinal gland or Crypts of Lieberkuhn to secrete digestive enzymes and villi/microvilli to increase surface area for maximum absorption of food. It also contain goblet cells to secrete mucus. Duodenal glands (or Brunner's glands) are located in the submucosal layer.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following four statements (A-D):

D. The innermost layer lining the lumen of the alimentary canal is the serosa.

How many of the above statements are wrong?
questions.solution:
Statements 1&2 are correct whereas statements 3&4 are incorrect.

The small intestine is the most important absorbing organ in the& GI tract. About 90% of nutrient absorption takes place in the small intestine.

Constipation: In constipation, the faeces are retained within the rectum as the bowel movements occur irregularly.

Gross calorific values& of fat is 8.8 kcal/gm.

Serosa is the outermost layer and is made up of a thin mesothelium (epithelium of visceral organs) with some connective tissues. The innermost layer lining the lumen of the alimentary canal is the mucosa.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The first site for observing chyme in the human gut is
questions.solution: The stomach stores the food for 4-5 hours. The food mixes thoroughly with the acidic gastric juice of the stomach by the churning movements of its muscular wall and is called the chyme. The proenzyme pepsinogen, on exposure to hydrochloric acid gets converted into the active enzyme pepsin, the proteolytic enzyme of the stomach. Pepsin converts proteins into proteoses and peptones (peptides).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The correct function of hormones of gastrointestinal tract is
options: gastrin is inhibitory to the gastric glands but excitatory to the gall bladder.
secretin is excitatory to pancreas but is inhibitory to the gastric glands.
cholecystokinin is excitatory to the gall bladder but is inhibitory to the pancreas.
pancreozymins is excitatory to the pancreas but is inhibitory to the gall bladder.
questions.solution:
Gastrin is secreted by stomach and acts on the stomach. It stimulates the gastric gland to release gastric juice.

Secretin is secreted by duodenum and acts on the pancreas, liver, and stomach. It is excitatory to pancrease but is inhibitory to the gastric glands.

CCK (Cholecystokinin) is also known as pancreozymins and is secreted from small intestine and cause& the release of digestive enzymes and bile from the pancreas and gallbladder, respectively.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The fatty liver syndrome is due to excessive intake of
questions.solution: Fatty liver is a condition that is also known as hepatic steatosis. It is observed due to the accumulation of fat in the liver. Having too much of fat in the liver can become a health problem. The chronic use of drugs and alcohol damages the liver in which the destruction of hepatocytes and fibroblasts is seen.&

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which part of the gut shows the negligible amount of absorption of substances?
questions.solution:
Absorption in the oesophagus is virtually nil.
Its role in digestion is simple: to convey boluses of food from the pharynx to the stomach.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When breastfeeding is replaced by less nutritive food low in proteins and calories; the infants below the age of one year are likely to suffer from
questions.solution: Marasmus is a nutrient deficiency disease in infants below 1 year of age that occurs when sufficient mother's milk is not given to the child. Prolonged starvation causes marasmus due to a generalized wasting of the body because of both energy and protein deficiency. The body becomes lean and weak, eyes depressed and skin wrinkled. Kwashiorkor is a disease caused by continued deficiency of proteins in diet although energy intake may be adequate. Rickets (in children) occurs due to deficiency of vitamin-D. Pellagra occurs due to deficiency of nicotinamide (vitamin-B_{3}).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: There is a valve present at the junction of
questions.solution: Small intestine consists of three parts: C Shaped duodenum, Jejunum and ileum. Ileum then continues as large intestine. The parts of large intestine are caecum, colon and rectum. Thus ileum is connected to the caecal part of large intestine. There is a valve seen here and is known as ileocaecal valve as this prevents backflow of matter once it has entered the caecum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The muscularis layer of alimentary canal has
options: inner circular and outer longitudinal muscles
inner longitudinal and outer circular muscles
inner smooth and outer skeletal muscles
inner skeletal and outer smooth muscles
questions.solution: The Alimentary canal consists of four layers. The innermost layer i.e. surrounding the lumen is the mucosa layer. This layer consists of epithelium, Lamina propria and muscularis mucosae. The second layer surrounding the mucosa layer is sub mucosa which consists of MALT (Mucosal associated lymphoid tissue). The third layer is the muscularis layer. This is made up of two layers of muscles. Inner layer of circular muscles and outer is of longitudinal muscles. These layers are responsible for peristalsis. The stomach shows extra oblique layer too as churning movements are also seen in the stomach. In stomach the oblique muscles form the inner layer, middle is by circular and outer layer is of longitudinal muscles. The outermost layer or the fourth layer is the serosa.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The pancreatic juice contains enzymes
options: trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases, amylases, lipases and nucleases.
trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases, aminopeptidases, amylases, lipases and nucleases.
trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases, aminopeptidases, amylases, lipases and nucleases, nucleotidases, nucleosidases.
trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases, amylases, lipases, pepsinogen and nucleases.
questions.solution: Pancreatic juice and bile open through a hepatopancreatic duct into the duodenum where intestinal juice also mixes with it. Duodenum is the site where maximum digestion takes place. First the pancreatic juice acts on the macromolecules and then intestinal juice acts on them to finally convert into micromolecules that can be readily absorbed. These are done with the help of various enzymes present in the juices. Pancreatic juice contains enzymes in an inactive form that become activated by enterokinase (an enzyme of the small intestine). The inactive enzymes are trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases, amylases, lipases, and nucleases. Enterokinase first activates trypsinogen to form trypsin and then this enzyme activates the other pancreatic enzymes. Trypsin, chymotrypsin, and carboxypeptidases act on proteins. Amylases act on starch. Lipases act on fats. Nucleases act on nucleic acids. Lipases are present in gastric juice, pancreatic juice and succus entericus too.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Common bile duct is form by the union of
options: common hepatic duct and cystic duct
left hepatic duct and cystic duct
questions.solution: Accessory glands in digestion are liver and pancreas. Ducts of these glands finally open into the duodenum. These ducts unite at various levels. The liver consists of right and left lobes through which righ and left hepatic ducts arise. These ducts collect bile formed by hepatic cells and unite and form a hepatic duct that further unites with the cystic duct of gall bladder. This is known as the common bile duct. This duct contains concentrated bile from gall bladder and dilute bile from liver. The common bile duct is also known as duct choledochus (chole means bile). This duct then unites with the duct of Wirsung (pancreatic duct) to form the hepatopancreatic duct that opens into the duodenum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The absorption of monosaccharide such as glucose in the small intestine occurs by:
questions.solution: The absorption of some monosaccharide such as glucose and some aminoacids may occur by all three possible ways.& Glucose is absorbed from lumen of small intestine by simple diffusion, facilitated transport as well as by an active transport method.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the process of digestion is CORRECT?

I. Carbohydrates in the chyme are hydrolyzed by pancreatic amylase into monosaccharides directly.

II. Nucleases in the intestinal juice act on nucleic acids to form nucleotides and nucleosides.
options: Both I and II are correct
Both I and II are wrong
I is correct and II is wrong
II is correct and I is wrong
questions.solution: Carbohydrates in the chyme are hydrolyzed to disaccharides by the pancreatic amylase. The starch is converted into isomaltose, maltose, and dextrins. The intestinal juice converts the disaccharide to monosaccharides. The nucleic acids are broken down to form nucleotides by the nucleases present in the pancreatic juice, these nucleotides are further reduced to form nucleosides by the intestinal juice with the enzyme nucleosidases and nucleotidases.&

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not correct?
questions.solution: Brunner's glands (or duodenal glands) are compound tubular submucosal glands found in that portion of the duodenum which is above the hepatopancreatic sphincter (Sphincter of Oddi). questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution:
Tooth enamel is the hard, outer surface layer of your teeth that serves to protect against tooth decay. In fact, tooth enamel is considered the hardest mineral substance in your body, even stronger than bone.

questions.solution: The small intestine is distinguishable into three regions, a ‘C’ shaped duodenum, a long coiled middle portion jejunum and highly coiled ileum. The opening of the stomach into the duodenum is guarded by the pyloric sphincter.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If for some reason our goblet cells become non-functional, it will adversely affect
options: secretion of sebum from the sebaceous glands
smooth movement of food down the intestine
questions.solution: Goblet cells, found in the intestinal mucosal epithelium, secrete mucus. the mucus lubricates the food for an easy passage. So, if for some reason, goblet cells become non-functional, it will adversely affect the smooth movement of food down the intestine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following forms the major part of the tooth and is covered by enamel?
questions.solution:
The structure of teeth can be divided into three regions:
a) Crown: The hard chewing surface covering of the teeth is made up of enamel which helps in the mastication of food. This enamel is the hardest substance of the human body. This enamel is non-living part of tooth. Below it the living part of tooth is present which is called as ameloblast dentine and it forms enamel. This dentine covers the cavity of tooth called as pulp cavity. Canaliculi connects pulp cavity to enamel.
b) Neck: It is formed by sockets and gums.
c) Root: It forms the part of pulp cavity. The pulp cavity contains the small cavity which provides nerves and blood capillaries to teeth and it enters tooth from an opening called as apical foreman. The hollow cavity of pulp is called as root canal. The outer covering of root is called as cementum. Cementum& connects the root with the jaw bone.

questions.solution: Dietry deficiencies of proteins and total food calories (carbohydrates) are widespread in many underdeveloped countries. It is commonly called protein-energy malnutrition (PEM) which causes Marasmus and Kwashiorkar in infants and children.

mature and smaller than normal erythrocytes

questions.q: Which of the following is false about villi?
options: They are small finger-like foldings in the small intestine.
They are supplied with a rich network of blood capillaries.
They are supplied with large lymph capillaries called lacteals.
They have numerous microvilli which give the appearance of ciliated epithelium.
questions.solution: The innermost layer lining the lumen of the alimentary canal is the mucosa. This layer forms irregular folds (rugae) in the stomach and small finger-like foldings called villi in the small intestine. The cells lining the villi produce numerous microscopic projections called microvilli giving a brush border appearance. These modifications increase the surface area enormously. Villi are supplied with a network of capillaries and a large lymph vessel called the lacteal.&

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A zymogen is an inactive substance which is made active with the help of different enzymes. Pepsinogen is secreted as a zymogen into the stomach to
options: change the pH of the stomach fluids to aid digestion.
prevent digestion of the gastric glands.
questions.solution: Pepsinogen is a proenzyme, which gets converted into enzyme pepsin when it comes in contact with hydrochloric acid in the stomach. Enzyme pepsin helps in the digestion of proteins. When pepsinogen is secreted in the stomach, it is in the form of zymogen. This is to prevent the digestion of the gastric glands by direct action of pepsinogen.
